```{webr}
#| include: false
#| autorun: true
# Lab machinery – the pre-computed specification universe and the helper
# functions the preregistration flow uses. Participants interact with
# prereg(), build_model(), run_spec() and report_result(); the results these
# print come from the committed grid of 2,520 pre-computed specifications,
# so no heavy model fitting happens in the browser.
.grid <- read.csv("data/spec_grid_full.csv")
.neg_framings <- c("mcomm", "mlib", "mneg")

.menu <- list(
  my_outcome     = c("mcosmo", "mutil", "mcomm", "mlib", "mpos", "mneg"),
  my_family      = c("gaussian", "beta"),
  my_predictor   = c("unemp", "growth"),
  my_pred_form   = c("raw", "log"),
  my_copredictor = c("none", "growth", "unemp"),
  my_estimator   = c("fe_twoway", "fe_country", "re", "pooled_cl"),
  my_sample      = c("all", "y2004_2008", "y2009_2013", "no_bailout", "no_GR_ES"),
  my_weights     = c("none", "n_cy")
)

.est_lab <- function(e) c(
  fe_twoway  = "two-way fixed effects (country + year)",
  fe_country = "country fixed effects",
  re         = "random effects",
  pooled_cl  = "pooled OLS, clustered by country")[[e]]

.check_choices <- function() {
  need <- names(.menu)
  missing <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(missing) > 0)
    stop("Not declared yet: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "),
         ". Fill in every choice in the preregistration cell and run it first.",
         call. = FALSE)
  if (!exists("claim_align"))
    stop("Also declare claim_align <- TRUE (the day's convention) in the preregistration cell.",
         call. = FALSE)
  ch <- lapply(need, function(k) get(k))
  names(ch) <- need
  for (k in need) {
    v <- ch[[k]]
    if (!is.character(v) || length(v) != 1 || !v %in% .menu[[k]])
      stop(sprintf("%s = \"%s\" is not on the menu. Options: %s.",
                   k, paste(v, collapse = ","),
                   paste(.menu[[k]], collapse = " | ")), call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (ch$my_estimator == "re" && ch$my_weights == "n_cy")
    stop("The random-effects estimator is never fitted with weights (the menu excludes re + n_cy). Set my_weights <- \"none\" or pick another estimator.",
         call. = FALSE)
  if (ch$my_predictor == "growth" && ch$my_pred_form == "log")
    stop("GDP growth enters raw only – it takes negative values, so the log is undefined. Set my_pred_form <- \"raw\".",
         call. = FALSE)
  if (ch$my_predictor == ch$my_copredictor)
    stop(sprintf("%s is already your claim-carrying predictor; my_copredictor must be \"none\" or the other measure.",
                 ch$my_predictor), call. = FALSE)
  ch
}

.lookup <- function(ch) {
  hit <- .grid[.grid$outcome == ch$my_outcome & .grid$family == ch$my_family &
               .grid$predictor == ch$my_predictor &
               .grid$pred_form == ch$my_pred_form &
               .grid$copredictor == ch$my_copredictor &
               .grid$estimator == ch$my_estimator &
               .grid$sample == ch$my_sample & .grid$weights == ch$my_weights, ]
  if (nrow(hit) != 1)
    stop("That combination is not in the pre-computed universe – check each choice against the menu comments.",
         call. = FALSE)
  hit
}

# the claim-alignment factor: negative framings are reverse-coded (1 - y),
# and growth's claim-expected sign is positive, so both flip the sign
.flip <- function(ch, hit)
  (if (hit$positive_outcome) 1 else -1) *
  (if (ch$my_predictor == "growth") -1 else 1)

.spec_line <- function(ch) {
  neg <- ch$my_outcome %in% .neg_framings
  paste0(ch$my_outcome, if (neg) "_ca" else "", " ~ ",
         ch$my_predictor, "(", ch$my_pred_form, ")",
         if (ch$my_copredictor != "none") paste0(" + ", ch$my_copredictor) else "",
         " | ", ch$my_estimator, " | ", ch$my_sample,
         " | w:", ch$my_weights, " | ", ch$my_family)
}

prereg <- function() {
  ch <- .check_choices()
  .lookup(ch)   # confirms the combination exists; the result stays unseen
  neg <- ch$my_outcome %in% .neg_framings
  cat("DECLARED – one specification, recorded before seeing its result:\n\n")
  cat("  outcome    :", ch$my_outcome,
      if (neg) "(negative framing – reverse-coded automatically)" else "", "\n")
  cat("  family     :", ch$my_family, "\n")
  cat("  predictor  :", ch$my_predictor, paste0("(", ch$my_pred_form, ")"),
      if (ch$my_predictor == "growth") "(claim-expected sign flipped automatically)" else "", "\n")
  cat("  copredictor:", ch$my_copredictor, "\n")
  cat("  estimator  :", .est_lab(ch$my_estimator), "\n")
  cat("  sample     :", ch$my_sample, "   weights:", ch$my_weights, "\n")
  cat("  claim_align:", isTRUE(claim_align), "\n\n")
  cat("These choices are now fixed for the rest of the session – the later\n")
  cat("cells read them from here. Copy the whole cell into wherever you keep\n")
  cat("your notes: that copy is your preregistration record.\n")
  invisible(ch)
}

build_model <- function(formula, estimator) {
  ch <- .check_choices()
  if (missing(formula) || !inherits(formula, "formula"))
    stop("The first argument must be a formula: outcome ~ predictor terms, unquoted.",
         call. = FALSE)
  lhs <- all.vars(formula[[2]])
  if (!identical(lhs, ch$my_outcome))
    stop(sprintf("Your formula's outcome is '%s' but you preregistered '%s'. The preregistration is binding – fix the formula, not the prereg.",
                 deparse(formula[[2]]), ch$my_outcome), call. = FALSE)
  main <- if (ch$my_predictor == "unemp" && ch$my_pred_form == "log")
    "log(unemp)" else ch$my_predictor
  want <- c(main, if (ch$my_copredictor != "none") ch$my_copredictor)
  got <- attr(terms(formula), "term.labels")
  if (!setequal(got, want))
    stop(sprintf("Right-hand side mismatch: you wrote { %s } but your preregistration implies { %s }.%s",
                 paste(got, collapse = ", "), paste(want, collapse = ", "),
                 if (main == "log(unemp)" && !"log(unemp)" %in% got)
                   " You preregistered the log form – write log(unemp) in the formula." else ""),
         call. = FALSE)
  if (missing(estimator) || !identical(estimator, ch$my_estimator))
    stop(sprintf("estimator = \"%s\" does not match your preregistered \"%s\".",
                 if (missing(estimator)) "" else estimator, ch$my_estimator),
         call. = FALSE)
  cat("Model accepted – it matches your preregistration exactly:\n")
  cat("  ", deparse(formula), ", estimated by ", .est_lab(estimator), "\n", sep = "")
  structure(list(choices = ch, formula = formula, estimator = estimator),
            class = "spec_ticket")
}

run_spec <- function(spec) {
  if (missing(spec) || !inherits(spec, "spec_ticket"))
    stop("Pass the object build_model() returned, e.g. run_spec(my_model).",
         call. = FALSE)
  now <- .check_choices()
  if (!identical(spec$choices, now))
    stop("The preregistration cell has changed since you built this model – rerun prereg() and build_model() so they agree.",
         call. = FALSE)
  ch <- spec$choices
  hit <- .lookup(ch)
  fl <- .flip(ch, hit)
  ca <- isTRUE(claim_align)
  stat_lab <- if (ch$my_family == "beta") "z" else "t"
  b <- hit$estimate; tv <- hit$statistic; r <- hit$r
  if (ca) { b <- fl * b; tv <- fl * tv; r <- fl * r }
  p <- 2 * pt(-abs(hit$statistic), hit$df)
  cat("Your preregistered specification, computed:\n\n")
  cat("  ", .spec_line(ch), "\n", sep = "")
  if (ca && ch$my_outcome %in% .neg_framings)
    cat("  (negative framing – reverse-coded automatically: claim_align = TRUE)\n")
  if (ca && ch$my_predictor == "growth")
    cat("  (growth predictor – sign convention flipped automatically: claim_align = TRUE)\n")
  if (!ca)
    cat("  (claim_align = FALSE: shown on each outcome's own scale; the class chart converts)\n")
  cat(sprintf("\n  b = %.5f   se = %.5f   %s = %.3f on %d df   p %s\n",
              b, hit$se, stat_lab, tv, hit$df,
              if (p < 0.001) "< 0.001" else sprintf("= %.3f", p)))
  aligned_r <- fl * hit$r
  cat(sprintf("  claim-aligned partial r = %.3f   (below zero supports the claim)\n",
              aligned_r))
  canon <- .grid[.grid$family == "gaussian" & .grid$predictor == "unemp", ]
  canon_rca <- canon$r * ifelse(canon$positive_outcome, 1, -1)
  cat(sprintf("\n  Placement: %.1f%% of the canonical 840 specifications support the claim\n",
              100 * mean(canon_rca < aligned_r)))
  cat("  more strongly than this one (the full universe holds 2,520).\n")
  invisible(list(b = b, se = hit$se, stat = tv, df = hit$df, n = hit$n,
                 r = aligned_r))
}

report_result <- function() {
  ch <- .check_choices()
  hit <- .lookup(ch)
  fl <- .flip(ch, hit)
  # the class chart lives on the claim-aligned scale, so the submission is
  # always aligned, whatever claim_align displays above
  b <- fl * hit$estimate; tv <- fl * hit$statistic; r <- fl * hit$r
  spec_label <- .spec_line(ch)

  FORM_ID <- "1FAIpQLSezoAEOnZUfP4pkfN28_XtEBwSyc2RLsXB-h8RPSegF7_t76A"
  field <- c(spec = "entry.832496914", b = "entry.1656311800", se = "entry.1337458262",
             t = "entry.1940779437", df = "entry.1682711955", n = "entry.1586392724",
             r = "entry.1660273001")
  value <- c(spec = spec_label, b = sprintf("%.5f", b),
             se = sprintf("%.5f", hit$se), t = sprintf("%.3f", tv),
             df = as.character(hit$df), n = as.character(hit$n),
             r = sprintf("%.3f", r))
  query <- paste(vapply(names(field), function(k)
    paste0(field[[k]], "=", utils::URLencode(value[[k]], reserved = TRUE)),
    character(1)), collapse = "&")
  url <- sprintf("https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/%s/viewform?usp=pp_url&%s",
                 FORM_ID, query)

  cat("Your submission (claim-aligned, straight from your preregistration):\n\n")
  cat("  spec:", spec_label, "\n")
  cat(sprintf("  b = %.5f | se = %.5f | %s = %.3f | df = %d | n = %d | r = %.3f\n\n",
              b, hit$se, if (ch$my_family == "beta") "z" else "t", tv,
              hit$df, hit$n, r))
  cat("Click the link below (or copy the URL) – the form opens with every\n")
  cat("field pre-filled; just press Send.\n\n")
  cat(url, "\n")
  htmltools::browsable(htmltools::tags$p(
    htmltools::tags$a(href = url, target = "_blank", rel = "noopener",
                      "Open the pre-filled submission form")))
}
```
:::


Five analysts reanalysed a claim from @Teney2016DoesEUEconomic for the Multi100 project [@AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness]; you are analyst no. 6. Read the full task description, the claim, and the five-analyst table of findings on the [Exercise overview](index.qmd) page (the [workshop slides](../slides/index.qmd) discuss the broader context of the project).

This page is the whole exercise, runnable in the browser: seven tasks that take you from vocabulary to a dot on the live class chart.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Task 1 – Concepts (warm-up while the engine loads)

**Before touching data, fix the vocabulary.** In the four scenarios below, three are doing one of our three R's; one is doing something else entirely. Read the four scenarios, then label each in the code cell below.

***Scenario 1:*** A reviewer reruns the authors' Stata `.do` file on the authors' data and gets a *different* coefficient from the one printed in the paper. This is an example of \_\_\_\_\_\_, even though what they *tried* to do failed.

***Scenario 2:*** The analyst uses the authors' submitted replication dataset, but they re-implement the model in R instead of Stata and centre the predictor. Is this a case of \_\_\_\_\_\_ or \_\_\_\_\_\_?

***Scenario 3: *** A preregistered team tests the identical hypothesis on a *separate, much larger* dataset chosen to be theoretically equivalent, and gets results that contradict the original. Their conclusion is that the original analysis has failed to \_\_\_\_\_\_.

***Scenario 4:*** Instead of the survey data used by the original authors, another researcher tests the same underlying idea on social-media texts using a machine-learning classifier method that the original never used. To their surprise, the authors' original findings prove \_\_\_\_\_\_ and the researcher concludes that they provide a reliable middle-range theory of the phenomenon they investigate.

Now, if the R engine has loaded, give it a test run by filling in the gaps in the same text in the code chunk below and run the code to see the output.

:::: {.solution exercise="vocab"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Answers – and the two traps

1.  **reproducibility** – rerunning the same code on the same data. Here it *failed* to match, but the activity is still reproducibility; "not reproduced" is the verdict.
2.  arguably still **reproducibility** (a grey area) – re-implementing on the same data in different software is technically a re-computation – but centring the predictor nudges toward **robustness**, not to mention that different software may have different implementations of the same estimators, so one must make sure they understand the functions they use.
3.  **replicability** – same question, independent new data chosen to be theoretically equivalent.
4.  **generalisability** – the impostor: new data *and* a new method at once. It is the fourth cell of the matrix, not one of the three we test today.
:::
::::


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Task 2 – Get the data and look at it

The **EU-frames dataset** (`EUframes_cy.csv`) is already loaded for you as `euframes`. It is the corrected country-year panel behind the whole exercise, and the copy this page loads is byte-identical to the one published in the analyst's fork on OSF (osf.io/6zqct – "Multi100 \| Teney_EurSocioRev_2016 \| Analyst_C6HJR", main folder); the official Multi100 archival record is at osf.io/8rtwe. Route 1 participants download the same file into an IDE workspace; in the browser it is pre-loaded so you can get straight to the analysis.

Run the cell below to inspect the panel. Edit it freely – this is your environment.


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
# How many countries, how many years, how big is the panel?
dplyr::glimpse(euframes)

cat("\nCountries:", dplyr::n_distinct(euframes$cntry),
    " Years:", dplyr::n_distinct(euframes$year),
    " Rows:", nrow(euframes), "\n")
```
:::


You should see **270 rows**, **27 countries**, **10 years** (2004–2013), and 13 columns. The outcome we care about first is `mcosmo` – the mean 'cosmopolitan' framing of the EU in each country-year (a 0–1 scale; the other framings and every column are described in the [codebook](../data/EUframes_cy_codebook.md)). The predictor is `unemp`, the annual unemployment rate; `growth` is annual GDP growth, and `n_cy` counts the survey respondents behind each row.

Now look at the outcome over time, one small panel per country:


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(euframes, aes(x = year, y = mcosmo)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey55") +
  geom_point(size = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ cntry, ncol = 6) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2004, 2008, 2013)) +
  labs(
    title = "Cosmopolitan EU framing by country, 2004–2013",
    x = NULL, y = "Mean cosmopolitan framing"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9)
```
:::


Most countries drift gently; a few move sharply around the 2009 crisis. That variation – within a country, over time – is exactly what the fixed-effects model in Task 3 uses.

## Task 3 – Reproduce the recorded result

This is the **reproducibility** check. Fit the two-way fixed-effects model the Multi100 Task-2 constraints point to:

```
mcosmo ~ unemp_c   with fixed effects for country and year
```

where `unemp_c` is the unemployment rate centred on its grand mean. The target is **t = −3.804** (df = 233, N = 270) – the value on record for analyst C6HJR in the Multi100 dataset.

The cell below is an exercise. Replace the blanks (`______`) with the missing code, then press "Run Code". Stuck? Open the hint; want to check? Open the solution.


::: {.cell setup='true' exercise='reproduce'}
```{webr}
#| setup: true
#| exercise: reproduce
euframes <- read.csv("data/EUframes_cy.csv")
```
:::



::: {.cell exercise='reproduce'}
```{webr}
#| exercise: reproduce
# 1. centre the unemployment rate on its grand mean
euframes$unemp_c <- euframes$unemp - ______

# 2. fit two-way fixed effects with fixest::feols
#    the part after the | adds the fixed effects
m1 <- feols(mcosmo ~ unemp_c | ______, data = euframes)

broom::tidy(m1)
```
:::


:::: {.hint exercise="reproduce"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Hint 1 – centring

To centre a variable on its grand mean, subtract the mean of the whole column:

``` r
euframes$unemp_c <- euframes$unemp - mean(euframes$unemp)
```

With fixed effects present this does not change the t-statistic, but it is the transformation the constrained specification asks for, so do it explicitly.
:::
::::

:::: {.hint exercise="reproduce"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Hint 2 – the fixed-effects syntax

In `fixest::feols`, the bar `|` separates the regression from the fixed effects. To add country and year fixed effects, list them after the bar separated by `+`:

``` r
feols(mcosmo ~ unemp_c | cntry + year, data = euframes)
```
:::
::::

:::: {.solution exercise="reproduce"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Fully worked solution

``` r
euframes$unemp_c <- euframes$unemp - mean(euframes$unemp)
m1 <- feols(mcosmo ~ unemp_c | cntry + year, data = euframes)
broom::tidy(m1)
```

You should get `estimate ≈ −0.00347`, `std.error ≈ 0.00091`, `statistic ≈ −3.80` – the recorded value reproduces from the published data and the published model. `feols` reports IID standard errors by default when two fixed-effect dimensions are present, which is why it matches the `plm` value to three decimals.
:::
::::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## The other number in the record – a story worth opening

There is a second number in this analysis's public trail: **t = −3.853**. It is what the *first* submitted pipeline produced, and the gap to the −3.804 you just reproduced has a story.

The as-submitted data-preparation script stacked sixteen Eurobarometer waves and read the EB 70.1 file (`ZA4819`) twice by mistake: once for 2008 (correct) and again in place of EB 72.4 (`ZA4994`) for 2009. The panel's 2009 rows were therefore a copy of the 2008 respondents – the two builds diverge on 2009 and nowhere else, and 2009 carried about half the respondents it should have. The analyst caught the slip during the project and corrected it; the recorded −3.804 comes from the corrected build – the very `EUframes_cy.csv` you are using.

The whole trail is public in the analyst's fork ([osf.io/6zqct](https://osf.io/6zqct/)): the `moreh_rep/` folder preserves the as-submitted pipeline; `moreh_rep_vAPR2025/` holds the corrected script – annotated "APRIL 2025 – Mistake in dataset here; the dataset associated with 'eb724' should be 'ZA4994_v3-0-0.dta'" – together with the exported corrected dataset; and the main folder now carries `EUframes_cy.csv` itself, the exact file this page loads. The official Multi100 component ([osf.io/8rtwe](https://osf.io/8rtwe/)) preserved only the earlier, uncorrected folder.

Coding can go wrong – even during a reanalysis. Keeping materials open and well documented is what lets a mistake be spotted and corrected. That is reproducibility working, not failing.
:::

## Task 4 – Estimand and DAG

Before fitting anything, say what you are trying to estimate, in words. A template you can adapt:

> The **unit-specific quantity** is the change in a country-year's mean cosmopolitan EU framing associated with a one-point change in that country's unemployment rate. The **target population** is EU member states over 2004–2013. The **aggregation** is the average of those unit-specific effects, holding fixed each country's time-invariant traits and each year's EU-wide shocks.

That last clause is a causal claim, and a DAG makes it checkable. If the [dagitty.net](https://www.dagitty.net/dags.html) page below doesn't load, navigate to that external site.

Paste the code below into the Model code field and update the graph:
<br>

```
dag {
unemployment [exposure]
framing [outcome]
country -> unemployment ; country -> framing
year -> unemployment ; year -> framing
unemployment -> framing
}
```


```{=html}
<iframe width="780" height="500" src="https://www.dagitty.net/dags.html" title="Dagitty"></iframe>
```

With the five committed edges, the minimal adjustment set is `{ country, year }` – exactly what a two-way fixed-effects model absorbs. That is no accident: the DAG and the Task 3 model encode the same identification claim. Add a `growth -> unemployment` and a `growth -> framing` edge and the set becomes `{ country, year, growth }` – now your model needs the co-predictor to match your beliefs. Write two sentences for your own notes: what do two-way fixed effects adjust for, and what can they **not** fix? (Hint: anything time-varying within a country that you have not measured.)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Task 5 – My preregistration

The point of preregistration is that you commit to a choice **before** you see what it does. It stops you quietly picking the specification that happens to give the answer you wanted. Here the commitment is real in a mechanical sense too: the choices you declare in this cell are remembered by the session, and every later cell reads them from here – the model builder will refuse code that deviates from them.

::: {.callout-important icon="false"}
## How the block maps to a real preregistration

*A real preregistration, shortened. Each numbered comment maps to a question in the OSF "Preregistration Template from AsPredicted.org" (the eight-question short form). Because you are reanalysing data that already exist, field 2 also stands in for the prior-knowledge section of the secondary-data template (van den Akker et al. 2021) – the part AsPredicted leaves out.*
:::

Make one choice on each axis of the [specification menu](spec-menu.qmd) – every axis is live, including the outcome family and the predictor – complete the dotted lines, then run the cell. `claim_align <- TRUE` is the day's convention, applied automatically: negative framings are reverse-coded (1 − y) and growth's claim-expected sign is flipped, so 'supports the claim' reads as a negative sign for everyone.


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
# ============================================================================
# MY PREREGISTRATION – one specification, declared before seeing its result
# ============================================================================
# 1. The claim I am testing: .................................................
# 2. The data + what I already know: EUframes_cy.csv (270 country-years,
#    public); I know the constrained baseline gives t = -3.804.
# 3. My one specification – one choice on each axis:

my_outcome     <- "mcosmo"     # mcosmo | mutil | mpos    (positive framings)
                               # mcomm  | mlib  | mneg    (negative framings)
my_family      <- "gaussian"   # gaussian | beta   (logit-link on the cell
                               #                    means; beta reports z)
my_predictor   <- "unemp"      # unemp | growth    (the claim-carrying measure)
my_pred_form   <- "raw"        # raw | log   (growth: raw only; centring or
                               #              z-scaling would leave t, r and p
                               #              unchanged - not separate analyses)
```

## Hint – from menu speak to model syntax

The formula uses the column names of `euframes`: the outcome you preregistered on the left of `~`, the predictor terms on the right. For the baseline declaration it is `mcosmo ~ unemp`; with the log form it would be `mcosmo ~ log(unemp)`; with a co-predictor, `mcosmo ~ unemp + growth`. The estimator is the menu code itself, in quotes: `"fe_twoway"`, `"fe_country"`, `"re"` or `"pooled_cl"`. You do not write the fixed-effects or clustering syntax here – the estimator code stands for it, and Task 3 showed what it expands to.
:::

Read the output like an analyst: the coefficient and its claim-aligned partial *r* (below zero supports the claim), and your placement – how much of the canonical 840-specification grid supports the claim more strongly than your choice does. The five Multi100 analysts run from about the 16th percentile (the most strongly claim-supporting) to about the 68th (near the null); your dot is about to join theirs.
